You might notice your child becoming harsher in how they talk"},{"line":81,"start":"00:06:17,960","end":"00:06:20,560","text":"or more secretive than usual."},{"line":82,"start":"00:06:20,560","end":"00:06:25,240","text":"They might quickly switch screens or become defensive when you walk past."},{"line":83,"start":"00:06:25,240","end":"00:06:31,960","text":"These signs do not prove cyberbullying, but they are a reason to start a calm conversation."},{"line":84,"start":"00:06:31,960","end":"00:06:36,520","text":"And another thing to look at is how they are day to day, offline."},{"line":85,"start":"00:06:36,520","end":"00:06:41,720","text":"If they are often unkind to their peers or often put others down, it does not automatically"},{"line":86,"start":"00:06:41,720","end":"00:06:46,720","text":"mean cyberbullying, but it is a sign that a conversation is needed."},{"line":87,"start":"00:06:46,720","end":"00:06:52,280","text":"And if you find out your child has hurt someone, starting calmly really helps."},{"line":88,"start":"00:06:52,280","end":"00:06:57,920","text":"It is often not easy, but if the conversation starts with blame or labels, children tend"},{"line":89,"start":"00:06:57,920","end":"00:07:05,560","text":"to shut down. What they learn may be, next time, don't get caught, rather than responsibility."},{"line":90,"start":"00:07:05,560","end":"00:07:09,400","text":"The goal is accountability without shame."},{"line":91,"start":"00:07:09,400","end":"00:07:14,120","text":"You could start with, I heard something might have happened and I want to understand what"},{"line":92,"start":"00:07:14,120","end":"00:07:18,080","text":"really happened rather than, why would you do that?"},{"line":93,"start":"00:07:18,080","end":"00:07:23,240","text":"The next step is helping them see the impact and this part really matters because many"},{"line":94,"start":"00:07:23,240","end":"00:07:30,200","text":"children will say, I was just joking or everyone else was doing it."},{"line":95,"start":"00:07:30,200","end":"00:07:36,000","text":"Instead of focusing only on rules, bring it back to how it felt for the other person."},{"line":96,"start":"00:07:36,000","end":"00:07:41,800","text":"You might ask something like, if that was said to you, how would you feel? That helps"},{"line":97,"start":"00:07:41,800","end":"00:07:44,840","text":"them begin to understand the impact."},{"line":98,"start":"00:07:44,840","end":"00:07:51,640","text":"The third step is repair, not hiding it, not avoiding it. Real growth is about fixing"},{"line":99,"start":"00:07:51,640","end":"00:07:54,960","text":"things, not just getting out of trouble."},{"line":100,"start":"00:07:54,960","end":"00:08:01,560","text":"Repair should be concrete, not just, I'm sorry. First, stop the harm, delete or correct"},{"line":101,"start":"00:08:01,560","end":"00:08:09,280","text":"harmful posts, ask others not to share them and report or remove fake accounts if needed."},{"line":102,"start":"00:08:09,280","end":"00:08:14,820","text":"Then support a proper apology that owns what happened. If a school or another family is"},{"line":103,"start":"00:08:14,820","end":"00:08:19,140","text":"involved, bring in adults to help repair safely."},{"line":104,"start":"00:08:19,140","end":"00:08:23,340","text":"This is something families work through together, not alone."},{"line":105,"start":"00:08:23,340","end":"00:08:28,260","text":"At the same time, take a step back and ask why this happened. There is usually something"},{"line":106,"start":"00:08:28,260","end":"00:08:29,780","text":"going on underneath."},{"line":107,"start":"00:08:29,780","end":"00:08:36,380","text":"Yeah, it could be peer pressure, wanting to fit in, feeling overwhelmed or reacting in"},{"line":108,"start":"00:08:36,380","end":"00:08:37,820","text":"the moment."},{"line":109,"start":"00:08:37,820","end":"00:08:43,540","text":"Once you understand that, why, it is easier to prevent it from happening again."},{"line":110,"start":"00:08:43,540","end":"00:08:49,900","text":"That brings us back to a few simple things. Clear boundaries, staying connected and modeling"},{"line":111,"start":"00:08:49,900","end":"00:08:51,980","text":"respect."},{"line":112,"start":"00:08:51,980","end":"00:08:56,540","text":"Children are always watching, even when we don't realise it. They notice how we talk"},{"line":113,"start":"00:08:56,540","end":"00:09:01,540","text":"about other people, handle disagreements and deal with conflict."},{"line":114,"start":"00:09:01,540","end":"00:09:06,500","text":"That's right, Jack. We can't stop everything from happening, but we can try to make sure"},{"line":115,"start":"00:09:06,500","end":"00:09:11,820","text":"that when something does happen, children know that there is somewhere safe they can go."},{"line":116,"start":"00:09:11,820","end":"00:09:16,620","text":"When children know that harm will not be ignored, but also that they will not be shamed"},{"line":117,"start":"00:09:16,620","end":"00:09:22,780","text":"for talking about it, they are more likely to own what happened and learn from it."},{"line":118,"start":"00:09:22,780","end":"00:09:28,740","text":"In the next episode, we'll talk about another tough topic, online sexual harm. We'll talk"},{"line":119,"start":"00:09:28,740","end":"00:09:33,380","text":"about what to watch for and what parents can actually do."},{"line":120,"start":"00:09:33,380","end":"00:09:33,820","text":"See ya!"}]

title: Protection From Online Sexual Harm
description: This episode explains how parents can respond when children face sexual risks online. It focuses on staying calm, reassuring children without shame or punishment, avoiding repeated probing, and giving clear guidance about safety,
transcript_text: [{"line":1,"start":"00:00:00,000","end":"00:00:15,000","text":"Welcome to 8 minutes of digital parenting. I'm Emily."},{"line":2,"start":"00:00:15,000","end":"00:00:17,000","text":"Hi, I'm Jack."},{"line":3,"start":"00:00:17,000","end":"00:00:21,000","text":"In our last episode, we talked about cyberbullying."},{"line":4,"start":"00:00:21,000","end":"00:00:23,000","text":"One thing we kept coming back to was this."},{"line":5,"start":"00:00:23,000","end":"00:00:29,000","text":"When something goes wrong online, it is not about rushing to decide who is right or wrong."},{"line":6,"start":"00:00:29,000","end":"00:00:34,000","text":"It's about being there with your child and working through the situation together."},{"line":7,"start":"00:00:34,000","end":"00:00:41,000","text":"Exactly. And if your child has hurt someone, ignoring it or going straight to scolding or punishment,"},{"line":8,"start":"00:00:41,000","end":"00:00:44,000","text":"usually does not create real change."},{"line":9,"start":"00:00:44,000","end":"00:00:51,000","text":"That's right. What helps is to help them see the impact, take responsibility and understand where the line is."},{"line":10,"start":"00:00:51,000","end":"00:00:56,000","text":"A quick note before we start. Today's topic is sensitive,"},{"line":11,"start":"00:00:56,000","end":"00:01:00,000","text":"but we'll keep the discussion practical and non-graphic."},{"line":12,"start":"00:01:00,000","end":"00:01:06,000","text":"The aim is not to raise an alarm, but to give families clear language and a calm plan."},{"line":13,"start":"00:01:06,000","end":"00:01:13,000","text":"If this episode raises concerns for you, support links are available on the podcast information page."},{"line":14,"start":"00:01:13,000","end":"00:01:20,000","text":"That's right. Today we're focusing on another online risk that children in years 7 to 9 can come across."},{"line":15,"start":"00:01:20,000","end":"00:01:27,000","text":"Sexual content or online contact that feels uncomfortable, secretive or pressured."},{"line":16,"start":"00:01:27,000","end":"00:01:34,000","text":"If a child is in immediate danger, contact emergency services or local police."},{"line":17,"start":"00:01:34,000","end":"00:01:40,000","text":"Many parents hear that and think, they're still so young and that reaction is completely understandable."},{"line":18,"start":"00:01:40,000","end":"00:01:47,000","text":"But the reality is, young people of this age can still come across this content quite easily."},{"line":19,"start":"00:01:47,000","end":"00:01:51,000","text":"Most of the time children are not actively searching for it."},{"line":20,"start":"00:01:51,000","end":"00:01:59,000","text":"It may pop up while they're doing ordinary things, watching videos, playing games, browsing or following a link."},{"line":21,"start":"00:01:59,000","end":"00:02:05,000","text":"It might be a pop up ad, a recommended video or even a link shared in a group chat."},{"line":22,"start":"00:02:05,000","end":"00:02:08,000","text":"Exactly. It can happen unexpectedly."},{"line":23,"start":"00:02:08,000","end":"00:02:15,000","text":"Some of this content can also send confusing messages such as the idea that relationships do not need respect,"},{"line":24,"start":"00:02:15,000","end":"00:02:21,000","text":"consent or care or that controlling or aggressive behaviour is normal."},{"line":25,"start":"00:02:21,000","end":"00:02:30,000","text":"Children can react in different ways. Some may feel curious, while others may feel uncomfortable, embarrassed, confused or scared."},{"line":26,"start":"00:02:30,000","end":"00:02:34,000","text":"None of these reactions mean that they have done something wrong."},{"line":27,"start":"00:02:34,000","end":"00:02:42,000","text":"An accidental exposure is different from pressure, grooming or threats, which need a more protective response."},{"line":28,"start":"00:02:42,000","end":"00:02:49,000","text":"That's right. And this is where many parents wonder, how do I explain this to a child in years 7-9?"},{"line":29,"start":"00:02:49,000","end":"00:02:54,000","text":"Parents may worry about giving too much detail or saying the wrong thing."},{"line":30,"start":"00:02:54,000","end":"00:03:02,000","text":"But saying nothing at all means children are left trying to figure it out on their own, which can make things more confusing."},{"line":31,"start":"00:03:02,000","end":"00:03:08,000","text":"One simple way to explain it is, some people call this pornography or adult sexual content."},{"line":32,"start":"00:03:08,000","end":"00:03:12,000","text":"It means sexual material that isn't meant for children."},{"line":33,"start":"00:03:12,000","end":"00:03:16,000","text":"It often doesn't show respectful or realistic relationships."},{"line":34,"start":"00:03:16,000","end":"00:03:21,000","text":"If you come across it, you're not in trouble and we can always talk about it."},{"line":35,"start":"00:03:21,000","end":"00:03:24,000","text":"You can also keep it non-shaming."},{"line":36,"start":"00:03:24,000","end":"00:03:31,000","text":"Curiosity about our bodies and relationships is normal, but not everything online is safe, accurate or healthy."},{"line":37,"start":"00:03:31,000","end":"00:03:38,000","text":"The point is not to frighten children. It is to give them clear words and a safe person to talk to."},{"line":38,"start":"00:03:38,000","end":"00:03:41,000","text":"Parents can also explain consent simply."},{"line":39,"start":"00:03:41,000","end":"00:03:48,000","text":"Consent means each person freely chooses, feels able to say no and can change their mind."},{"line":40,"start":"00:03:48,000","end":"00:03:53,000","text":"It should never involve pressure, threats, tricks or secrecy."},{"line":41,"start":"00:03:53,000","end":"00:03:57,000","text":"And no one should ask a young person for sexual images."},{"line":42,"start":"00:03:57,000","end":"00:04:00,000","text":"But how might parents notice that something like this has happened?"},{"line":43,"start":"00:04:00,000","end":"00:04:04,000","text":"Often parents first notice small changes in behavior."},{"line":44,"start":"00:04:04,000","end":"00:04:10,000","text":"A child may suddenly turn their screen away or quickly close a page when someone walks past."},{"line":45,"start":"00:04:10,000","end":"00:04:18,000","text":"They might become tense, withdrawn or unusually quiet while watching videos or playing games that used to feel relaxed."},{"line":46,"start":"00:04:18,000","end":"00:04:28,000","text":"When parents notice something like that, unless there is an immediate safety concern, they do not need to immediately check messages or search through their device."},{"line":47,"start":"00:04:28,000","end":"00:04:32,000","text":"What often helps the most is opening a gentle conversation."},{"line":48,"start":"00:04:32,000","end":"00:04:42,000","text":"For example, have you ever seen something online that made you feel uncomfortable or has anyone ever asked you to keep a conversation secret?"},{"line":49,"start":"00:04:42,000","end":"00:04:52,000","text":"Some children may avoid talking about what they are doing online, change the subject quickly or show embarrassment or anxiety when asked simple questions."},{"line":50,"start":"00:04:52,000","end":"00:05:02,000","text":"These signs do not always mean something serious has happened, but they can suggest the child may have seen or experienced something that they were not yet ready for."},{"line":51,"start":"00:05:02,000","end":"00:05:11,000","text":"That's right. You can continue by asking, have you heard people talking about pornography or nude images online?"},{"line":52,"start":"00:05:11,000","end":"00:05:17,000","text":"What have you heard? Or do you have any questions about things you've seen or heard online?"},{"line":53,"start":"00:05:17,000","end":"00:05:25,000","text":"Many children stay quiet because they worry that telling the truth might lead to anger, shame or losing their device."},{"line":54,"start":"00:05:25,000","end":"00:05:33,000","text":"It can help to keep three simple ideas in mind. The first is to stay calm and helping your child feel steady."},{"line":55,"start":"00:05:33,000","end":"00:05:41,000","text":"Feeling shocked or anxious is natural, but even pausing before responding can make the conversation safer."},{"line":56,"start":"00:05:41,000","end":"00:05:48,000","text":"Parents might reassure their child by saying, you're not in trouble or I'm really glad you told me."},{"line":57,"start":"00:05:48,000","end":"00:05:53,000","text":"When children feel safe from immediate punishment, they're more willing to talk honestly."},{"line":58,"start":"00:05:53,000","end":"00:05:58,000","text":"The second idea is focusing on the child's feelings rather than the details."},{"line":59,"start":"00:05:58,000","end":"00:06:06,000","text":"Many parents want to know exactly what was seen, but asking children to describe it again can sometimes be distressing."},{"line":60,"start":"00:06:06,000","end":"00:06:15,000","text":"Instead, ask, how did it make you feel? Scared, uncomfortable, embarrassed or confused? Then listen carefully."},{"line":61,"start":"00:06:15,000","end":"00:06:20,000","text":"If needed, help the child close the page or leave the app together."},{"line":62,"start":"00:06:20,000","end":"00:06:25,000","text":"The third idea is helping the child know what to do next time."},{"line":63,"start":"00:06:25,000","end":"00:06:33,000","text":"Keep the plan simple. If something feels off, look away, close the app, don't reply and come tell me."},{"line":64,"start":"00:06:33,000","end":"00:06:40,000","text":"If someone is pressuring or threatening you, don't send anything more and tell an adult straight away."},{"line":65,"start":"00:06:40,000","end":"00:06:44,000","text":"That's it. Keep the plan simple and memorable."},{"line":66,"start":"00:06:44,000","end":"00:06:49,000","text":"Uh-huh. It is normal for young people to be curious about their bodies or relationships."},{"line":67,"start":"00:06:49,000","end":"00:06:56,000","text":"Curiosity is not the problem. Secrecy, pressure, threats and shame are the danger signs."},{"line":68,"start":"00:06:56,000","end":"00:07:00,000","text":"It can help to separate responses into three situations."},{"line":69,"start":"00:07:00,000","end":"00:07:05,000","text":"Accidental exposure means closing it and talking."},{"line":70,"start":"00:07:05,000","end":"00:07:10,000","text":"Pressure or threats means stopping responding and getting an adult."},{"line":71,"start":"00:07:10,000","end":"00:07:15,000","text":"Grooming or extortion means official help is needed."},{"line":72,"start":"00:07:15,000","end":"00:07:20,000","text":"Before we wrap it up, one safety point matters."},{"line":73,"start":"00:07:20,000","end":"00:07:29,000","text":"If explicit images of a young person are involved, parents should not save, screenshot, forward or share the images."},{"line":74,"start":"00:07:29,000","end":"00:07:37,000","text":"Record user names, URLs, dates and platform details where safe and seek advice from e-safety,"},{"line":75,"start":"00:07:37,000","end":"00:07:43,000","text":"the Australian Centre to counter child exploitation, the school or police."},{"line":76,"start":"00:07:43,000","end":"00:07:49,000","text":"Across this series, we've tried to shift digital parenting away from fear and conflict"},{"line":77,"start":"00:07:49,000","end":"00:07:53,000","text":"and towards connection, understanding and calm support."},{"line":78,"start":"00:07:53,000","end":"00:07:59,000","text":"Online risks do not disappear completely, but children are safer when they know what to do"},{"line":79,"start":"00:07:59,000","end":"00:08:02,000","text":"and feel able to come to you."},{"line":80,"start":"00:08:02,000","end":"00:08:06,000","text":"If you've made it this far, you are already doing something that matters."},{"line":81,"start":"00:08:06,000","end":"00:08:11,000","text":"Across these eight episodes, we've talked about different kinds of online risk,"},{"line":82,"start":"00:08:11,000","end":"00:08:17,000","text":"content, contact, conduct and privacy or data risks"},{"line":83,"start":"00:08:17,000","end":"00:08:22,000","text":"and what families can do before things happen and when something goes wrong."},{"line":84,"start":"00:08:22,000","end":"00:08:28,000","text":"Digital parenting is not about ticking boxes, it is something you build over time."},{"line":85,"start":"00:08:28,000","end":"00:08:30,000","text":"Yeah, it is a relationship."},{"line":86,"start":"00:08:30,000","end":"00:08:36,000","text":"That's right, every time you listen, stay calm and stick with your child,"},{"line":87,"start":"00:08:36,000","end":"00:08:40,000","text":"especially when something goes wrong, you are helping to build trust."},{"line":88,"start":"00:08:40,000","end":"00:08:44,000","text":"And of course, every family is different."},{"line":89,"start":"00:08:44,000","end":"00:08:48,000","text":"Eight short episodes simply cannot cover everything."},{"line":90,"start":"00:08:48,000","end":"00:08:53,000","text":"So if something feels tricky or serious, it is completely OK to reach out for extra help,"},{"line":91,"start":"00:08:53,000","end":"00:08:59,000","text":"such as the school, e-safety, the Australian Centre to counter child exploitation"},{"line":92,"start":"00:08:59,000","end":"00:09:01,000","text":"or other support services."},{"line":93,"start":"00:09:01,000","end":"00:09:05,000","text":"Links to these services can be found on the podcast information page."},{"line":94,"start":"00:09:05,000","end":"00:09:08,000","text":"You do not have to figure this all out on your own."},{"line":95,"start":"00:09:08,000","end":"00:09:10,000","text":"That's right, Jack."},{"line":96,"start":"00:09:10,000","end":"00:09:13,000","text":"If there is just one thing to take away from this, it is this."},{"line":97,"start":"00:09:13,000","end":"00:09:16,000","text":"You do not have to handle this perfectly."},{"line":98,"start":"00:09:16,000","end":"00:09:20,000","text":"What matters most is that your child knows they can come to you."},{"line":99,"start":"00:09:20,000","end":"00:09:22,000","text":"Yeah, they're not dealing with things on their
